sections.description: A self-hosted, context-aware website guide with customer-owned AI billing and WordPress data.
sections.changelog:
1.6.4

  • Move the note under the message box above it, where it is read before typing rather than after the answer.

1.6.3

  • Resume a cross-page action in the message that started it, instead of adding a second progress row to a later reply.

1.6.2

  • Report the questions Nika could not answer, so you can write the page visitors were looking for.

1.6.1

  • Do not report arriving at a section when the page opened but the anchor is not on it.

1.6.0

  • Place the highlight label beside the highlight instead of inside it, so it cannot cover the content it names.
  • Keep a highlight up when the visitor closes the panel to look at it.

1.5.9

  • No plugin changes. Released alongside a website correction so both editions stay on one version.

1.5.8

  • Answer a repeated or refined request instead of replying that it was handled earlier, and resolve what a short follow-up like highlight it refers to.

1.5.7

  • Universal reads a licence of its own, so both editions answer to the same packages.

1.5.6

  • Export a configuration and apply it to another site. The AI key and licence key never leave in the file.

1.5.5

  • Credit Nika with one small line under the message box. Business and Agency can turn it off.

1.5.4

  • Name the package a licence is on, and mark the controls a larger package includes rather than hiding them.

1.5.3

  • Ask abatchan.com for updates with your licence key, so a build is only ever handed to the person who bought it.

1.5.2

  • Add a licence key field. Nika runs with or without one; a key brings updates and support, and never changes what visitors see.

1.5.1

  • Move the last two descriptive notes behind their question mark, and put the exempt-IP actions under the field they act on.

1.5.0

  • Open a field note above its question mark, so it points at what it explains instead of covering the input.

1.4.9

  • Reveal a field note on keyboard focus, not only on click or hover.

1.4.8

  • Move descriptive field notes behind a question mark beside the label, keeping the ones that affect what you type on screen.

1.4.7

  • Follow the configured bubble shadow colour on hover as well, not only at rest.

1.4.6

  • Keep the highlight's label under the chat panel instead of floating over it.

1.4.5

  • Style the highlight's label on the page itself, so it is a positioned pill rather than unstyled text that pushed the layout around.

1.4.4

  • Drop the separate link colour setting: links follow the accent, so it was one more field saying the same thing.

1.4.3

  • Restore the note under the message box to its intended spacing, which 1.4.2's own margin reset had flattened.

1.4.2

  • Add a link colour setting so links inside answers follow your palette instead of the built-in indigo.
  • Colour the highlight's close control from the configured accent like every other guide surface.
  • Pin the guide's own margins so a theme or browser default cannot shift its chrome.
  • Prefer the content a navigation or footer label points at, rather than the menu entry that repeats it.

1.4.1

  • Preserve complete cross-page highlight actions when a visitor clicks a saved destination link.
  • Trust verified anchors, wait for dynamically rendered targets, and resolve each site's live accessible DOM without customer-specific selector maps.
  • Support portable data-nika-target and data-nika-label overrides for ambiguous custom components.
  • Rank targets by the kind of thing named in the request, so "the Business package" highlights the whole card instead of its buy button.
  • Dim the rest of the page while a highlight is up, so the answer reads as the answer.
  • Repaint the highlight ring in real time when the site switches between light and dark.
  • Let the visitor dismiss a highlight early with a close control, the Escape key, or a press on the page.
  • Draw the highlight ring in the brand accent, thinner, and inside anything that clips its overflow.

1.4.0

  • Use a clean rounded highlight outline without an added glow shadow.
  • Style section labels as compact pills using the saved accent colour.

1.3.9

  • Prefer exact targets in the main page content over duplicate navigation and footer labels.

1.3.8

  • Highlight visible package cards, exact prices, and complete sections without altering heading text.
  • Keep rings visible against the surrounding surface and remove internal route language from conversation history.
